reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) mentions CrAl coatings as a research direction and states that Al must be considered for high-temperature steam oxidation, but provides no specific data or mechanistic evidence supporting the formation of a protective alumina layer at the Cr–Zr interface, its stability under both normal and accident conditions, or its ability to limit interdiffusion and improve adhesion. The key premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Aluminum addition to Cr coating forms a protective alumina layer at the Cr–Zr interface
This alumina layer limits Cr–Zr interdiffusion
The alumina layer remains stable and protective under both ~300°C PWR water and ~1100–1200°C steam
Reduced interdiffusion prevents coating delamination and premature failure
Cr–Al coating outperforms pure Cr coating in oxidation resistance and adhesion
